summary_paragraph: A woman with primary sclerosing cholangitis and Child-Pugh class B cirrhosis was admitted for observation following a routine EGD and colonoscopy due to new right upper quadrant pain and elevated liver enzymes. She had no signs of infection, and blood cultures were negative. Liver function tests improved during the stay, and her pain resolved without antibiotic treatment. During EGD, one esophageal varix with red markings was banded prophylactically, and mild portal hypertensive gastropathy was noted. She remained hemodynamically stable, tolerated a regular diet, and was discharged home in stable condition with a two-week course of sucralfate and instructions to continue all home medications. A repeat EGD is scheduled in six weeks, and colonoscopy biopsies are pending.
